📌 Main Purpose

This is a sneak peek at one component of Godly Hand — a full all-in-one NPC creator coming to Nexus. The Debug Commands tool solves a specific problem every NPC modder hits during testing: remembering console commands, looking up event IDs, and typing the same things into SMAPI over and over.

If you have ever tested a custom NPC, you know the loop. You edit a schedule or an event, reload the game, open the SMAPI console, try to remember your manifest UniqueID for patch reload, type it wrong, fix it, then try to remember which event ID you need to trigger, look it up in your JSON, type debug ebi and the ID, get it wrong by one digit, and do it all again. Every single test cycle.

Import your manifest → import your events file → click to copy. That's it.

⚙️ Features

📂 Manifest import with auto-fill
Click Locate manifest.json and select it from your mod folder. The tool reads your UniqueID and generates your patch reload command automatically. Handles manifests with trailing commas, // line comments, and /* block comments */ — the kind of formatting you find in real mods like Ridgeside Village and Amon.

🔍 Event file import with search
Import your Regular_Events.json or Marriage_Events.json. The tool parses every event entry, extracts the event ID, map name, heart requirements, day-of-week conditions, and dating or marriage preconditions. Browse the full list or search by any of those fields. Click an event to add it to your scene list.

🎬 Scene registry with one-click copy
Build a list of every event you want to test. Each scene gets a label you choose — something like "6-heart rainy town" or "marriage kitchen" — and the debug ebi command generates automatically. Click Copy and paste it straight into the SMAPI console.

📋 Patch reload and patch summary
Your patch reload command is always visible at the top, ready to copy. Patch summary is there too — one click when you need to check what loaded and what didn't.

📄 Export to .txt
Download a plain text file with your patch reload, patch summary, and every scene trigger laid out cleanly. Keep it open in Notepad while testing so you never have to switch windows to look up an ID.

⚠ Mod structure warning
Not all mods put their events in the same place. If you import a file and the tool finds zero events, a popup explains what happened and why — some authors put events inside content.json, split them across include files, or use non-standard target paths. You can always add event IDs manually.

📥 Installation

This tool runs entirely in your browser. There is nothing to install.

HTML version — recommended for most users
Download GodlyHand_DebugCommands.html
Open it in Chrome, Firefox, or Edge
Done — no setup required

JSX version — for Claude / React environments
Download GodlyHand_DebugCommands.jsx
Drop it into Claude.ai or any React sandbox and run it

Both versions are identical in functionality. No internet connection required after downloading.

⭐ How to Use

Opening the Tool
Take the GodlyHand_DebugCommands.html file and either:
Drag and drop it into your browser
Right-click → Open with → Choose your browser

Loading Your Manifest
Click Locate manifest.json and select the file from your mod folder. Your UniqueID fills in automatically and the patch reload command appears. You can also type the UniqueID manually if you know it — format is AuthorName.ModName.

Importing Events
Click Import Events JSON and select your events file — typically Regular_Events.json or Marriage_Events.json from your mod's Assets/Date folder. The tool reads every event and shows them in a searchable dropdown. Click any event to add it to your scene list.

If the tool can't find events in the file, it will tell you. Some mods structure their data differently — check how the author laid out their files. You can always type event IDs in manually.

Building Your Scene List
Label each scene with something you'll recognise fast. The debug ebi command generates from the event ID. Click Copy and paste it into the SMAPI console. Stand near the relevant map before triggering — events silently fail if you're in the wrong location.

Exporting
Click Export Debug Text File and you get a .txt with everything — patch reload, patch summary, and all your scene triggers with labels. Keep it open next to SMAPI while you test.

📋 Requirements

SMAPI
The Stardew Valley modding API. Required to run any console command. Get it at smapi.io.

Content Patcher
Required for patch reload and patch summary to work. Most custom NPC mods already depend on it.

A modern browser
Chrome, Firefox, or Edge. No internet connection required after downloading the file.
